purpose: The single sanctioned crossing between the public portal estate and the internal platform is named in portal-wiring.json as ECM_DOCS_INTAKE, and tests/portal-wiring.test.mjs asserted that it 'is deployed and reads Portal Registry'. That assertion passed. It was reading a superseded export.
method: Exports grouped by workflow_identity.internal_name rather than by display name, then compared on exportedAtUtc. Every one of the 60 files in docs/reference/flow-contracts/deployed/ carries exportedAtUtc, so the ordering is read from the captures themselves and not inferred.

exports.status: LIVE — the later capture of the same workflow

finding.itIsOneFlow: Not an inference. The 2026-08-31 paste-target resolution already established this id as one flow renamed and rebuilt in place, and used it as its decisive finding that the CG_* names are renames rather than new flows. What follows from it for the bridge was not drawn.
finding.soTheState: The workflow this repository calls ECM_DOCS_INTAKE is, as of its latest export, named CG_Upload_Endpoint, serves the portal's UPLOAD endpoint, and performs NO Portal Registry read.

whyTheCheckPassedAnyway: scripts/verify-portal-wiring.mjs resolved a flow by display name across every export in the directory. Both files carry the same workflow and different names, so findFlow('ECM_DOCS_INTAKE') matched the 2026-08-19 copy and reported the bridge healthy from it. The check was not wrong about the file it read; it was reading a file that had been superseded five days later.

whatIsNowTrue.afterTheFix: The sweep groups exports by workflow_identity.internal_name and keeps the latest by exportedAtUtc; the rest are reported as supersededExports rather than silently used. Definitions read moves 60 to 59.

whatThisDoesNotEstablish: Whether the Portal Registry read still exists in the tenant under some other flow. Only two deployed exports touch Portal Registry at all — this workflow's superseded copy, and CG_Writeback_Endpoint, which both reads and patches it. Nothing here says the agency intended the read to move there.

Whether the rebuild was deliberate. A 2-action feed becoming a 9-action upload endpoint under a new name is consistent with a deliberate repurposing and with an accidental overwrite, and the exports cannot separate the two.
What the flow contains today. The latest capture is 2026-08-24, a week old.
consequenceForThePaste: EXECUTION_GUIDE section 5.2 directs Portal_UPLOAD_ECM_DOCS at this workflow id, which is correct for UPLOAD and is the same flow portal-wiring.json calls the bridge. Whatever the bridge is meant to be, the UPLOAD paste writes over it. This must be settled before the paste, not after.
howToSettleIt: Export df7ddff1-9275-4f23-acf6-e169525f4e2f from the environment and read it. Then decide whether the intake feed still exists anywhere, and if it does not, whether D6's one-crossing argument still holds. Record ids only — a trigger URL is a bearer credential.
